<!-- ─── STEP 1: FORK & CLONE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
<div class="bg-white border-b border-gray-100 py-12 px-6">

           style="background:#6B0D1A;">1</div>
      <div>
        <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-gray-950">Fork &amp; Clone</h2>
        <p class="text-sm text-gray-500 mt-0.5">Get your own copy of the repository.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="space-y-6 pl-[52px]">

      <div>
        <p class="text-sm font-semibold text-gray-800 mb-2">Fork on GitHub</p>

        </p>
        <a href="https://github.com/Lawrence-lugs/digital_eee_upd/fork"
           target="_blank"
           class="inline-flex items-center gap-1.5 text-sm font-semibold px-4 py-2 rounded-lg border transition-colors"

          Fork on GitHub ↗
        </a>

<!-- ─── STEP 2: SET UP ENVIRONMENT ───────────────────────────────────────────── -->
<div class="bg-gray-50 border-b border-gray-100 py-12 px-6">
  <div class="max-w-3xl mx-auto">

    <div class="flex items-center gap-4 mb-7">
      <div class="flex-shrink-0 w-9 h-9 rounded-full text-white font-bold text-sm flex items-center justify-center"
           style="background:#6B0D1A;">2</div>
      <div>
        <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-gray-950">Set Up Your Local Environment</h2>
        <p class="text-sm text-gray-500 mt-0.5">
          Three options — all end with a live preview server that auto-reloads on save.
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="pl-[52px]">

      <!-- TAB BUTTONS -->
      <div class="flex flex-wrap gap-2 mb-5">
        <button id="tab-vscode" onclick="switchTab('vscode')"
                class="text-sm font-medium px-4 py-2 rounded-lg border cursor-pointer"
                style="background:#6B0D1A; color:white; border-color:#6B0D1A;">
          VS Code + Dev Container
        </button>
        <button id="tab-docker" onclick="switchTab('docker')"
                class="text-sm font-medium px-4 py-2 rounded-lg border cursor-pointer"
                style="background:white; color:#374151; border-color:#d1d5db;">
          Docker + Terminal
        </button>
        <button id="tab-local" onclick="switchTab('local')"
                class="text-sm font-medium px-4 py-2 rounded-lg border cursor-pointer"
                style="background:white; color:#374151; border-color:#d1d5db;">
          Local Install
        </button>
      </div>

      <!-- ── VS CODE PANEL ── -->
      <div id="panel-vscode">
        <div class="bg-white rounded-xl border border-gray-200 p-6">
          <p class="text-sm text-gray-500 mb-5 italic">
            Recommended for most contributors. VS Code detects the devcontainer configuration
            and sets up the full build environment automatically — no manual installation needed.
          </p>
          <ol class="space-y-5 text-sm list-none p-0 m-0">

            <li>
              <strong class="text-gray-800">Install prerequisites</strong>
              <ul class="mt-2 ml-5 list-disc space-y-1.5 text-gray-600">
                <li>
                  <a href="https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/" target="_blank"
                     class="underline" style="color:#6B0D1A;">Docker Desktop</a>
                  — launch it and confirm the engine is running (whale icon in your taskbar)
                </li>
                <li>
                  <a href="https://code.visualstudio.com/" target="_blank"
                     class="underline" style="color:#6B0D1A;">Visual Studio Code</a>
                </li>
                <li>
                  The
                  <a href="https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode-remote.remote-containers"
                     target="_blank" class="underline" style="color:#6B0D1A;">Dev Containers</a>
                  extension for VS Code
                </li>
              </ul>
            </li>

            <li>
              <strong class="text-gray-800">Open the cloned folder in VS Code</strong>
              <div class="mt-2 bg-gray-900 text-gray-100 rounded-lg p-4 overflow-x-auto">
                <pre style="margin:0; background:transparent; border:none; padding:0; white-space:pre;">code digital_eee_upd</pre>
              </div>
              <p class="mt-1.5 text-xs text-gray-500">
                Or use <strong>File → Open Folder</strong> and select the cloned directory.
              </p>
            </li>

            <li>
              <strong class="text-gray-800">Reopen in Container</strong>
              <p class="mt-2 text-gray-600 leading-relaxed">
                VS Code shows a notification in the bottom-right: <em>"Reopen in Container"</em>.
                Click it. If you missed it, open the Command Palette
                (<kbd class="bg-gray-100 border border-gray-300 rounded px-1.5 py-0.5 text-xs font-mono">Ctrl+Shift+P</kbd>
                or
                <kbd class="bg-gray-100 border border-gray-300 rounded px-1.5 py-0.5 text-xs font-mono">Cmd+Shift+P</kbd>
                on Mac) and run <strong>Dev Containers: Reopen in Container</strong>.
              </p>
              <p class="mt-2 text-gray-600">
                The first build pulls the container image — this takes a few minutes.
                Subsequent reopens are instant.
              </p>
            </li>

            <li>
              <strong class="text-gray-800">Start the preview server</strong>
              <p class="mt-2 text-gray-600 mb-2">
                Open a terminal inside VS Code
                (<kbd class="bg-gray-100 border border-gray-300 rounded px-1.5 py-0.5 text-xs font-mono">Ctrl+`</kbd>)
                and run:
              </p>
              <div class="bg-gray-900 text-gray-100 rounded-lg p-4 overflow-x-auto">
                <pre style="margin:0; background:transparent; border:none; padding:0; white-space:pre;">quarto preview</pre>
              </div>
              <p class="mt-1.5 text-xs text-gray-500">
                VS Code will auto-forward the port and offer to open the preview in your browser.
                The page reloads automatically whenever you save a file.
              </p>
            </li>

          </ol>
        </div>
      </div>

      <!-- ── DOCKER TERMINAL PANEL ── -->
      <div id="panel-docker" style="display:none;">
        <div class="bg-white rounded-xl border border-gray-200 p-6">
          <p class="text-sm text-gray-500 mb-5 italic">
            For terminal users who do not want to use VS Code. Uses the same container image
            as the devcontainer, so the environment is identical.
          </p>
          <ol class="space-y-5 text-sm list-none p-0 m-0">

            <li>
              <strong class="text-gray-800">Install Docker Desktop</strong>
              <p class="mt-2 text-gray-600">
                Download
                <a href="https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/" target="_blank"
                   class="underline" style="color:#6B0D1A;">Docker Desktop</a>
                for your OS. Launch it and wait for the Docker engine to be running
                before continuing.
              </p>
            </li>

            <li>
              <strong class="text-gray-800">Pull the container image</strong>
              <div class="mt-2 bg-gray-900 text-gray-100 rounded-lg p-4 overflow-x-auto">
                <pre style="margin:0; background:transparent; border:none; padding:0; white-space:pre;">docker pull ghcr.io/lawrence-lugs/quartolatex:latest</pre>
              </div>
            </li>

            <li>
              <strong class="text-gray-800">Run a container with the repo mounted</strong>
              <p class="mt-2 text-gray-600 mb-2">
                Run this command from inside the cloned <code class="bg-gray-100 px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded text-xs">digital_eee_upd</code> directory:
              </p>
              <div class="bg-gray-900 text-gray-100 rounded-lg p-4 overflow-x-auto">
                <pre style="margin:0; background:transparent; border:none; padding:0; white-space:pre;">docker run -it --rm \
  -v "$(pwd):/workspace" \
  -w /workspace \
  -p 4848:4848 \
  ghcr.io/lawrence-lugs/quartolatex:latest bash</pre>
              </div>
              <p class="mt-1.5 text-xs text-gray-500">
                This drops you into a bash shell inside the container with your repo files mounted.
                Any changes you make on your machine are immediately visible inside the container.
              </p>
            </li>

            <li>
              <strong class="text-gray-800">Start the preview server inside the container</strong>
              <div class="mt-2 bg-gray-900 text-gray-100 rounded-lg p-4 overflow-x-auto">
                <pre style="margin:0; background:transparent; border:none; padding:0; white-space:pre;">quarto preview --port 4848 --host 0.0.0.0</pre>
              </div>
              <p class="mt-1.5 text-xs text-gray-500">
                Open
                <a href="http://localhost:4848" target="_blank"
                   class="underline" style="color:#6B0D1A;">http://localhost:4848</a>
                in your browser. The preview reloads automatically on save.
              </p>
            </li>

          </ol>
        </div>
      </div>

      <!-- ── LOCAL INSTALL PANEL ── -->
      <div id="panel-local" style="display:none;">
        <div class="bg-white rounded-xl border border-gray-200 p-6">
          <p class="text-sm text-gray-500 mb-5 italic">
            No Docker? Install Quarto and the Python environment directly on your machine.
          </p>
          <ol class="space-y-5 text-sm list-none p-0 m-0">

            <li>
              <strong class="text-gray-800">Install Quarto</strong>
              <p class="mt-2 text-gray-600">
                Download the installer for your OS from
                <a href="https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/" target="_blank"
                   class="underline" style="color:#6B0D1A;">quarto.org/docs/get-started</a>.
              </p>
            </li>

            <li>
              <strong class="text-gray-800">Install Miniforge</strong>
              <p class="mt-2 text-gray-600">
                Miniforge is a lightweight conda distribution that includes the fast
                <code class="bg-gray-100 px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded text-xs">mamba</code>
                package solver. Download from
                <a href="https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge" target="_blank"
                   class="underline" style="color:#6B0D1A;">github.com/conda-forge/miniforge</a>.
              </p>
            </li>

            <li>
              <strong class="text-gray-800">Create and activate the Python environment</strong>
              <p class="mt-2 text-gray-600 mb-2">
                Run these commands from inside the cloned repository directory:
              </p>
              <div class="bg-gray-900 text-gray-100 rounded-lg p-4 overflow-x-auto">
                <pre style="margin:0; background:transparent; border:none; padding:0; white-space:pre;">mamba env create -f .devcontainer/env.yml
mamba activate numerical_sims</pre>
              </div>
            </li>

            <li>
              <strong class="text-gray-800">Start the preview server</strong>
              <div class="mt-2 bg-gray-900 text-gray-100 rounded-lg p-4 overflow-x-auto">
                <pre style="margin:0; background:transparent; border:none; padding:0; white-space:pre;">quarto preview</pre>
              </div>
              <p class="mt-1.5 text-xs text-gray-500">
                Quarto will print the local URL in the terminal output — open it in your browser.
                The preview reloads automatically on save.
              </p>
            </li>

          </ol>
        </div>
      </div>

    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- ─── STEP 3: EDIT OR ADD A PAGE ───────────────────────────────────────────── -->
<div class="bg-white border-b border-gray-100 py-12 px-6">
  <div class="max-w-3xl mx-auto">

    <div class="flex items-center gap-4 mb-7">
      <div class="flex-shrink-0 w-9 h-9 rounded-full text-white font-bold text-sm flex items-center justify-center"
           style="background:#6B0D1A;">3</div>
      <div>
        <h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-gray-950">Edit or Add a Page</h2>
        <p class="text-sm text-gray-500 mt-0.5">Pages are plain Markdown files. Any text editor works.</p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="pl-[52px] space-y-7">

      <!-- What is a .qmd -->
      <div>
        <p class="text-sm font-semibold text-gray-800 mb-2">
          What is a <code class="bg-gray-100 px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded text-xs">.qmd</code> file?
        </p>
        <p class="text-sm text-gray-600 leading-relaxed">
          A Quarto Markdown file — just plain Markdown with a short YAML header at the top.
          Standard Markdown syntax (headings, lists, images, tables, code blocks) all work out
          of the box. You can also embed raw HTML anywhere for more complex layouts.
        </p>
      </div>

      <!-- Where pages live -->
      <div>
        <p class="text-sm font-semibold text-gray-800 mb-3">Where pages live</p>
        <div class="bg-gray-50 border border-gray-200 rounded-lg overflow-hidden text-sm">
          <table class="w-full">
            <thead>
              <tr class="border-b border-gray-200 bg-gray-100">
                <th class="text-left px-4 py-2.5 text-xs font-semibold text-gray-500 uppercase tracking-wide w-1/2">Location</th>
                <th class="text-left px-4 py-2.5 text-xs font-semibold text-gray-500 uppercase tracking-wide">Contents</th>
              </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody class="divide-y divide-gray-100">
              <tr class="bg-white">
                <td class="px-4 py-3 font-mono text-xs text-gray-700">pages/logicLabs/</td>
                <td class="px-4 py-3 text-gray-600">Logic Labs (lab1.qmd – lab6.qmd and supporting files)</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td class="px-4 py-3 font-mono text-xs text-gray-700">pages/verilogCrashCourse/</td>
                <td class="px-4 py-3 text-gray-600">Verilog Crash Course chapters</td>
              </tr>
              <tr class="bg-white">
                <td class="px-4 py-3 font-mono text-xs text-gray-700">pages/</td>
                <td class="px-4 py-3 text-gray-600">Standalone pages (e.g. about.qmd)</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <td class="px-4 py-3 font-mono text-xs text-gray-700">static_apps/</td>
                <td class="px-4 py-3 text-gray-600">Self-contained HTML tools (not rendered by Quarto)</td>
              </tr>
            </tbody>
          </table>
        </div>
      </div>

      <!-- Minimal page template -->
      <div>
        <p class="text-sm font-semibold text-gray-800 mb-2">Minimal page template</p>
        <p class="text-sm text-gray-600 mb-3">
          Create a new <code class="bg-gray-100 px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded text-xs">.qmd</code>
          file anywhere in the tree. The only required part is the YAML frontmatter at the top:
        </p>
        <div class="bg-gray-900 text-gray-100 rounded-lg p-4 text-sm overflow-x-auto">
          <pre style="margin:0; background:transparent; border:none; padding:0; white-space:pre;">---
title: "My Page Title"
---

## Section Heading

Write your content using standard Markdown.

![An image caption](images/my-image.png)</pre>
        </div>
        <p class="mt-2 text-xs text-gray-500">
          The preview server will pick up the new file automatically — no restart needed.
        </p>
      </div>

      <!-- Navbar note -->
      <div class="bg-amber-50 border border-amber-200 rounded-lg p-4">
        <p class="text-sm font-semibold text-amber-800 mb-1">Adding your page to the navbar</p>
        <p class="text-sm text-amber-700 leading-relaxed">
          If you want your page to appear in the top navigation, add an entry to
          <code class="bg-amber-100 px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded text-xs">_quarto.yml</code>
          under <code class="bg-amber-100 px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded text-xs">website.navbar.left</code>.
          If you're not sure how, skip it — maintainers can wire up the navigation during PR review.
        </p>
      </div>

    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="bg-gray-50 border-b border-gray-100 py-12 px-6">

    <div class="pl-[52px] space-y-6">

          <pre style="margin:0; background:transparent; border:none; padding:0; white-space:pre;">git add .
git commit -m "Add: brief description of your change"
git push origin main</pre>

        <p class="text-sm font-semibold text-gray-800 mb-2">Open the pull request on GitHub</p>

      <!-- Auto-deploy note -->
      <div class="bg-blue-50 border border-blue-200 rounded-lg p-4">
        <p class="text-sm font-semibold text-blue-800 mb-1">What happens after merge</p>
        <p class="text-sm text-blue-700 leading-relaxed">
          The live site at
          <a href="https://digital.eee.upd.edu.ph" target="_blank"
             class="underline">digital.eee.upd.edu.ph</a>
          tracks the <code class="bg-blue-100 px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded text-xs">main</code> branch.
          Once your PR is reviewed and merged, the site rebuilds automatically and your
          content appears live within minutes.
        </p>
      </div>

    </div>
  </div>
</div>

    </a>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- ─── TAB SWITCHING SCRIPT ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── -->
<script>
function switchTab(name) {
  var tabs = ['vscode', 'docker', 'local'];
  tabs.forEach(function(id) {
    var panel = document.getElementById('panel-' + id);
    var btn   = document.getElementById('tab-' + id);
    if (id === name) {
      panel.style.display = 'block';
      btn.style.setProperty('background-color', '#6B0D1A', 'important');
      btn.style.setProperty('color', 'white', 'important');
      btn.style.setProperty('border-color', '#6B0D1A', 'important');
    } else {
      panel.style.display = 'none';
      btn.style.setProperty('background-color', 'white', 'important');
      btn.style.setProperty('color', '#374151', 'important');
      btn.style.setProperty('border-color', '#d1d5db', 'important');
    }
  });
}
</script>
